scope.description: What it **learns** from: how far back, and which conversations. Scope only grows.

scope.growOnlyNote: Scope only grows: unchecking does not delete what it already learned, nor shrink the scope — the graph and profile have already used those messages. To really remove data, use General › Wipe this channel's data.

attention.title: Persona listening scope
attention.note: Which conversations the persona **watches** for new messages — real-time only, no backfill. Separate from the learning scope above: you can turn this off any time (nothing gets deleted), because it stores no history.

attention.empty: No conversations picked — the persona currently evaluates new messages from **all** authorized conversations.

dataWipe.action: Clear this channel's signed-in account data
dataWipe.hint: Reset everything for the **currently signed-in account on this channel**: its corpus, indexes, graph and downloaded files, and sign it out. **Other channels under the same account are untouched.** You'll need to authorize, confirm your identity and pick a learning scope again. Irreversible.

dataWipe.confirmDetail: Everything collected on this channel by the **currently signed-in account** is permanently deleted, and that channel is signed out. Other channels are unaffected. This cannot be undone.
dataWipe.countFailed: Could not count — you can still proceed, but without a total.
dataWipe.willDelete: Will delete {{rows}} rows (messages, indexes and run traces)
dataWipe.resets: After clearing you will need to: authorize again, confirm your identity, pick a learning scope, and set up the persona again.
dataWipe.confirmAction: Delete permanently and sign out of this channel

workLayer.title: Work-layer extraction
workLayer.description: Uses the model to extract your scope of ownership, workflow, output preferences and hard-won conclusions from chat and documents, and writes them into the digital twin's skill package. Off by default.

ingestIntervals.title: Collection intervals
ingestIntervals.description: Polling interval per collection channel. Saving re-attaches collection in place and applies immediately.

hints.probeBaseMs: Fetches conversation-level change markers only (unread counts and last-message timestamps); roughly 0.7s per round. This is the base interval, not the effective one: adaptive backoff halves the rate when a round exceeds half the interval, so observed values may exceed what you set.
hints.probeMaxMs: Upper bound for adaptive backoff. Past this point the probe stops slowing down and raises a status-page warning instead — unbounded backoff degrades into probing once every few hours.
hints.activeScanMs: Walks the full conversation directory in descending activity order, compares against local watermarks, and issues targeted top-ups only for those behind. The incremental probe returns only conversations with unread markers (~13% coverage measured); this tier covers its blind spot. Fixed cost per round is one cached directory call plus one aggregate query — independent of conversation count.
hints.pullMs: Paginates a time window across all conversations to cover the probe's blind spot (read conversations don't appear in the unread list). A round can reach hundreds of pages and holds the collection lock exclusively, so short intervals crowd out sending and targeted top-ups.
hints.minutesMs: This endpoint has no time filter, so every round is a full enumeration at fixed cost — shorter intervals only add waste. Meetings are sparse events and don't warrant high frequency.
hints.documentsMs: A round covers workspace enumeration, recursive node traversal, and body backfill — substantially heavier than the message channel. Documents change slowly and carry no second-level visibility requirement.
hints.graphBuildMinIntervalMs: At least this long between two graph builds. NOT a fixed schedule — it will not build without enough new data, and enough data still waits out this gap. A build recomputes the whole graph, so keep it sparse.

ingestIntervals.note: Second-level visibility for new messages comes from the event stream and probe-triggered targeted top-ups, not from raising the full-pagination rate.
